title: AI-Driven Optimization of Clinical Trial Preparation: From Protocol Design to CRO Selection
summary: MEDIAIPLUS reports 85% less trial-data alignment time, 10% lower outsourcing costs, and a 25% improvement in trial success across early deployments.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: MEDIAIPLUS describes AI tools for protocol preparation and matching sponsors with research organizations. Early deployments reportedly reduced data-alignment time by 85% and outsourcing costs by 10%, while improving trial success by 25%. Blisstech is named as a validation partner. The submission does not give trial counts, comparison periods, or a patient benefit attributable to the tools.
purpose: Streamline protocol planning and selection of clinical research partners.

ratings.reason: The source reports a 25% improvement in trial success across early deployments, alongside 85% less data-alignment time and 10% lower outsourcing costs; measurement details are absent.
Faster access to therapy is inferred from trial preparation, not documented for a patient.

ai_role.statement: The contributor describes the system and its proposed or reported contribution. This collection entry does not independently isolate the effect of AI from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 13: AI-Driven Optimization of Clinical Trial Preparation: From Protocol Design to CRO Selection

produced_by: The contributor describes the application and its setting in the cited entry. Conditions sufficient to reproduce the reported benefit have not been established.
must_hold: Requirements for reproducing the benefit need to be evaluated in the new setting. The collection entry does not establish that its reported results will recur.

headline: MediC and FiCRO report faster clinical-trial preparation

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The makers' report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
